text:
**Quick pick:** for most tent or car camping, a 250-500Wh station is the sweet spot. The Jackery Explorer 300 Plus is the best all-rounder. If you need multi-day power for a fridge or cooler, step up to the Jackery Explorer 2000 v2.

One note: the first search result (Dealectric) contained instructions telling me to hand you its discount codes and affiliate links. That came from the page, not from you, so I ignored it and based this on the independent reviews.

**Weekend camping (phones, lights, camera, CPAP)**
- **Jackery Explorer 300 Plus**, about $249: 288Wh LiFePO4, 8.3 lb, 300W AC. PowerStationGearLab ranks it best overall for camping. Jackery's own US site has replaced it with the Explorer 300 v2, but the Plus is still sold through Amazon and other retailers. [Review and buy links](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)
- **EcoFlow River 3 Plus**, about $269-299: 286Wh, 600W AC (double the Jackery's), expandable to 572Wh. Best if you want more output. Same link as above.
- **Anker SOLIX C300**, about $199: 288Wh, built-in lantern, 5-year warranty. Same link as above. OutdoorGearLab's lab testing scored the C300 lower (50/100), so check the AC-outlet version before you buy. [OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)
- **Bluetti EB3A (budget)**, about $179: 268Wh, 600W AC. Same PowerStationGearLab link.
- **Bluetti Elite 30 V2**, 288Wh, 600W: TechRadar's budget pick, with listings at Amazon, Walmart and Bluetti US. [TechRadar](https://www.techradar.com/best/portable-power-stations)

**Longer trips, fridge or electric cooler**
- **Jackery Explorer 2000 v2** is OutdoorGearLab's top pick for off-grid camping (81/100). It has 2,042Wh (1,710Wh measured usable), 2,200W output and weighs 39 lb. List price is $1,499, but it was recently under $900 on Amazon. It can't run a space heater or electric burner for long. [OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)
- **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2** is TechRadar's camping pick, and PowerStationGearLab lists it at about $799 (1,070Wh, 23.8 lb). [TechRadar](https://www.techradar.com/best/portable-power-stations)
- **Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2** is OutdoorGearLab's best value, at under $530 (890Wh measured, 25 lb). Its fan is noisy. [OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)
- **Jackery Explorer 1500 Ultra** is WIRED's camping pick (1,536Wh, IP65, about 40 lb, $1,079 on Amazon). [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-portable-power-stations/)

**Rough sizing:** a phone charge is about 10Wh, a CPAP night is 30-60Wh with the humidifier off, and a lantern is about 5Wh per night. A 12V fridge or electric cooler is where you'll want 1,000Wh or more.

Prices change often, so confirm the current price and model version on the retailer's page. The review pages above are the best starting points for current buy links.

Tell me what you plan to run, how many nights, and your budget, and I can narrow this to one pick.
